long_biography.plain_text:
At Manacor Tennis Club, Toni Nadal began coaching his nephew Rafael when he was four. The boy also excelled at football, but his father eventually asked him to choose one sport so his schooling would not suffer. He selected tennis, turned professional at 15 and won the French Open on his first appearance at 19.

Nadal’s left-handed forehand, heavy topspin and relentless movement made him especially dominant on clay, yet his reach extended across every major surface. He completed a career Grand Slam and won Olympic gold in singles and doubles for Spain. Repeated injury comebacks shaped his later seasons before his last professional match at the 2024 Davis Cup Finals.

At Manacor Tennis Club, Toni Nadal began coaching his nephew Rafael when he was four. The boy also excelled at football, but his father eventually asked him to choose one sport so his schooling would not suffer. He selected tennis, turned professional at 15 and won the French Open on his first appearance at 19.

Nadal’s left-handed forehand, heavy topspin and relentless movement made him especially dominant on clay, yet his reach extended across every major surface. He completed a career Grand Slam and won Olympic gold in singles and doubles for Spain. Repeated injury comebacks shaped his later seasons before his last professional match at the 2024 Davis Cup Finals.
